DATE: August 28, 2024
SUBJECT: Agreement No. 47854 for Workday Implementation and Maintenance
Services with PowerPlan, Inc.
SUMMARY
The proposed Agreement No. 47854 (Agreement) is to procure software implementation
and maintenance services, and a subscription to PowerPlan’s licensed software
products in the PowerPlan cloud hosted environment for LADWP’s Business Asset
Accounting and Depreciation System. The term of this agreement is for a five-year
period beginning September 15, 2024, and it is for an amount not to exceed $8,200,000
(budgeted). The term of the Agreement will begin on September 15, 2024, to align with
the start date of the licenses needed for the software. The Agreement is the result of
Request for Sole Source Proposal No. 90758.
City Council approval is not required.
RECOMMENDATION
It is recommended that the Board of Water and Power Commissioners adopt the
attached Resolution authorizing the award of this Agreement to PowerPlan, Inc.
ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED
LADWP selected Workday, Inc. (PO 47652, BR 021 167) as its Enterprise Resource
Planning Project (ERP) solution in 2021. Financial Services Organization worked
closely with Workday consultants to replace PowerPlan software and implement
Workday's Business Assets module. During the Workday implementation phase, a
decision was made by key internal stakeholders to maintain PowerPlan as the
Department’s Business Asset Accounting module and integrate the software to
Workday financial Modules to meet LADWP’s complex operating requirements. This
decision to remain with the PowerPlan solution was based on a concern that the
Workday solution may not be well-suited to handle the complexity of LADWP’s
operating requirements for asset accounting.

The Agreement is for a term of five (5) years and an amount not to exceed $8.2 million.

BACKGROUND
The Department has billions of dollars in assets that it accounts for in both the Power
Fund and the Water Fund. These include generating stations, transmission lines, poles,
towers, fixtures, water mains, trunklines, meters, and service lines. Both funds use the
composite units of accounting for assets as opposed to individual assets due to the
volume. Back in approximately 2002-2003, the Department became aware that the
cumulative annual depreciation for some composite units exceeded the book value of
the assets. While the Department did record depreciation annually it did not have a
software solution to record these transactions cumulatively.
Prior to issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for depreciation software, the Department
also issued an RFP for a depreciation study to help us determine the most accurate
depreciation rates to use in the new planned system. Deloitte and Touche was selected
from the RFP for the depreciation study. Once that study was completed an RFP was
issued for the software and PowerPlan was selected as the best solution (Agreement
No. 47394-5). The implementation of the solution was a large effort and required

integration with the Department’s other systems to capture expenditures and
retirements.
The PowerPlan software was first implemented by the Department and the PowerPlan
consultants in 2008. Since 2008, the Department has worked with PowerPlan to
upgrade the software to its latest versions to keep up with changing technologies and to
benefit from new releases. In 2010, the Department upgraded the software from
version 9.0 to version 10.2 (Contract 49007-1). After four years, the Department
upgraded to version 2015.2 (Contract 41119-6), and recently completed the upgrade to
version 2022.1 in November 2022 (Contract 44504-3).
Current PowerPlan Applications Used by LADWP
The current PowerPlan application is an on-premises solution. LADWP licenses the use
of PowerPlan’s Project and Asset Accounting Products with the following functionalities:
Asset Accounting: tracks and keeps detailed records of Power and Water assets,
enables classification of asset records by vintage and by Federal Energy Regulatory
Commission and California Public Utilities Commission regulatory accounts.
Depreciation: applies group depreciation on assets, from in-service through
retirement.
Month-End Close: prepares journal entries to be sent to LADWP General Ledger
system.
Reporting: reports on monthly asset activity, asset posting transactions,
depreciation and amortization calculations, and ad-hoc Net Book Value and
Depreciation Forecasting reports used by Budget and Financial planning. Reports
for Water System (Aqueducts and Wells) and Power System (Open Access
Transmission Tariff).
Future PowerPlan Applications Used by LADWP
As part of the ERP, PowerPlan will need to be integrated with the future ERP system,
Workday. The system will also be moving from an on-premises solution to PowerPlan’s
Cloud-Hosted Subscription environment. In addition to the above PowerPlan Project
and Asset Accounting products, LADWP intends to add the following PowerPlan
product and functionalities:
Charge Repository: used for transaction management and data warehousing and
stores large volume of transactions for system integrations.
Project Unitization: enables the automatic generation of asset records, ties the
asset records to project details.

Asset Retirement Obligation: tracks and calculates journal entries for the liability,
deferred outflows, and amortization of deferred outflows associated with LADWP’s
AROs.
Lessee and Lessor Accounting: manage and report on leasing agreements,
process lease calculations for month-end processing and creation of journal entries.
ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION
Determine item is exempt pursuant to California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
Guidelines Section 15060 (c)(2). In accordance with this section, an activity is not
subject to CEQA if it will not result in a direct or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical
change in the environment. The proposed agreement to procure software
implementation and maintenance services, and a subscription to PowerPlan’s licensed
software products will not result in any direct or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical
change in the environment, therefore, this activity is not subject to CEQA.

Resolution No.
WHEREAS, the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) proposes to
enter into Agreement No. 47854 (Agreement) with PowerPlan, Inc. (PowerPlan) for
Workday Implementation and Maintenance Services for a term of five years; and
WHEREAS, LADWP requires a sole source agreement because PowerPlan has
proprietary knowledge, expertise and programming source code to maintain and
integrate its software to Workday financial modules as part of LADWP’s ERP solution;
and
WHEREAS, LADWP evaluated PowerPlan’s proposal, and PowerPlan has reviewed the
services to be provided and incorporated in this Agreement and represents that it has
the qualifications, expertise, skills and abilities to perform such work.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that LADWP proposes to enter into the
Agreement with PowerPlan in an amount not to exceed $8,200,000.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that pursuant to City Charter Section 1022, the Board of
Water and Power Commissioners (Board) finds that it is more feasible to have the work
performed by an independent contractor.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Agreement, approved as to form and legality by
the City Attorney, and filed with the Secretary of the Board, is hereby approved.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Chief Accounting Employee of LADWP, upon
proper certification, is authorized and directed to draw demands on the Power Revenue
Fund, in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and this Resolution.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the President or Vice President, or the General
Manager, or such person as the General Manager shall designate in writing, and the
Secretary, Assistant Secretary, or the Acting Secretary of the Board are hereby
authorized and directed to execute said Agreement for and on behalf of LADWP.

SUBJECT: Amendment No. 1 to Agreement Nos. 47677A and 47677B for
Proprietary Professional, Technical, and Repair Services and Parts
with GE Vernova International LLC and GE Vernova Operations LLC
SUMMARY
The proposed Amendment No. 1 (Amendment) to Agreement Nos. 47677A and 47677B
(Agreements) allows LADWP to continue procuring specialized services and Original
Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) parts from GE Vernova International LLC (GEVI) and
GE Vernova Operations LLC (GEVO). LADWP's generation fleet is largely composed of
GEVI, steam and gas units, and GEVO, aeroderivative units. This Amendment will
support the reliable operation of these units, allowing LADWP to provide dependable
power generation to the City of Los Angeles.
GEVI and GEVO have proprietary equipment, tools, and the necessary knowledge to
provide professional and technical assistance for inspections, diagnostics, repairs,
equipment tuning, and regulatory compliance testing. These services are critical to
ensure the highest level of reliability and availability of LADWP's General Electric (GE)
fleet. This Amendment will increase the not-to-exceed amount by $105,000,000, from
$160,000,000 to $265,000,000 (budgeted) to address unanticipated expenditures
mainly attributed to catastrophic generating unit failures. The term of the Agreements
will remain five years. All other terms and conditions will remain the same.
Los Angeles City Council approval is not required.
RE COMMENDATION
It is recommended that the Board of Water and Power Commissioners (Board) adopt
the attached Resolution approving the Amendment to the Agreements with GEVI and
GEVO.
ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED
An alternative to this Amendment would be to process one-time sole source purchase
orders for parts and services on a case-by-case basis. However, the process of creating
individual General Manager- and Board-awarded purchase orders would likely delay
projects and extend unit outages, causing operational challenges and financial losses in
the form of revenue loss, and incurred expenses. When GE-manufactured turbine­
generator units are unavailable, LADWP incurs significant costs. As an example, ii can
cost LADWP up to $9,200,000 per day if there is a failure of the largest GE combined
cycle system. These costs include the expense of purchasing replacement power for
system reliability. In addition, delays caused by processing one-time sole source orders
may lead to a loss of electric reliability standards compliance, potentially resulting in
regulatory fines. Another alternative to the Amendment is to prepare new Agreements
with GEVI and GEVO. However, this option would require at least 18 months to award,
potentially creating a long gap in services. Furthermore, ii is not possible to train
LADWP personnel to perform these services due to the proprietary procedures,
information, and tooling involved. Without this Amendment, there will be adverse
impacts to the Power System's generation fleet reliability.
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
The Amendment will increase the cumulative not-to-exceed amount by $105,000,000
from $160,000,000 to $265,000,000 (budgeted).

BACKGROUND
LADWP owns, operates, and maintains GEVI and GEVO units at all in-basin electric
Generating Stations. In an effort to supply reliable power to the City of Los Angeles,
LADWP must conduct scheduled outages for the inspection, maintenance, and repair of
its generation fleet. In addition, LADWP also performs emergency repairs during forced
outages when generating units break down.
Amendment No. 1 to Agreement Nos. 47677A and 47677B I October 21, 2024 Page 2
From the inception of the Agreements, various unanticipated expenditures have
occurred, mostly due to multiple catastrophic generating unit failures, necessitating the
procurement of replacement parts, spares, and mandatory upgrades. As a result,
contract expenditures to date have exceeded original estimated costs. In the past two
years, Haynes Generating Station (HnGS) Units 13 and 15, and Harbor Generating
Station (HGS) Unit 14 suffered blade liberation events, causing extensive damage and
costing the LADWP $18.1 million to repair the gas turbines. GE is continuing to
complete its root cause analysis on the failure events to assist in preventing future
similar events; however, in the interim, LADWP has modified the way it operates and
maintains its units with guidance from GE. Other large unexpected purchases include
approximately $14.9 million for gas turbine parts for HnGS Units 11-16, $4.9 million for
gas turbine nozzles for Scattergood Generating Station Units 6-7, and $6.2 million for
generator stator repairs at the Castaic Power Plant. These additional unforeseen
purchases were required to address potential blade liberation events on other
aeroderivative engines and to complete critical repairs based on discovery work not
accounted for during contract development.
Additionally, HGS Units 1 and 2 were subject to updated stack emissions limits required
by South Coast Air Quality Management District Rule 1135, with a compliance deadline
of January 1, 2024. In order to upgrade gas turbines to comply with requirements by the
stipulated deadline, LADWP issued GE a task order with a total cost of $19.0 million.

generation to the City of Los Angeles through the expiration of the current Agreements
while a new set of replacement agreements are developed.
These Agreements lessen the financial and operational impacts associated with forced
and scheduled outages by bringing the generating units back in-service as fast as
possible. The Agreements are also particularly important for performing emergency
repairs during unexpected forced outages. GE field engineers and technicians can be
immediately contacted and expeditiously brought on-site to provide the proprietary
services and parts necessary to restore LADWP's units back in service. Without
adequate funds in the Agreements, LADWP is at risk of incurring large financial losses
and operational difficulties during planned and unplanned unit outages, as repair
assistance and proprietary parts would not be immediately available. The work
performed under these Agreements will be assigned using a Task Order System. The
Task Order(s) will be issued by the Contract Administrator, and the work performed will
be monitored for completion prior to approval of the invoice payment. The Contract
Administrator will be responsible for controlling the costs within the expenditure limit of
the Agreements.
Both GEVI and GEVO have performed satisfactorily on the previous agreements.
ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION
Determine item is exempt pursuant to California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
Guidelines Section 15060(c)(3). In accordance with this section, an activity is not
subject to CEQA if it does not meet the definition of a project. Section 15378(b)(4)
states that government fiscal activities which do not involve any commitment to any
specific project which may result in a potentially significant physical impact on the
environment do not meet that definition. Therefore, the cost of this Amendment to
furnish and deliver services and parts for LADWP's GEVI and GEVO generation fleet is
not subject to CEQA.

The proposed Contract No. 0676 (Contract) is to furnish and deliver GPS and OEM

exceed $11,352,127 (budgeted). The Contract is a result of a competitive bid process.
The Contract will allow Fleet and Aviation Services (Fleet Services) to incorporate GPS
and vehicle telematics to effectively monitor vehicle data, predictive analytics, vehicle
utilization, electric vehicle (EV) charging data, and emissions data. The emissions
telematics data will be used to meet regulatory compliance testing requirements for
agencies like the California Bureau of Automotive Repair Testing Program (BAR CTP),
California Bureau of Automotive Repair Clean Truck Check Heavy Duty Inspection
(Clean Truck Check HD I/M), and other regulatory agencies.
City Council approval is not required.
RECOMMENDATION
It is recommended that the Board of Water and Power Commissioners adopt the
attached Resolution authorizing the award of Contract No. 0676 to Samsara Networks,
Inc. (Samsara), the lowest responsive bidder for Group A and B.
ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED
No alternatives were considered at this time.
Fleet Services will continue as is and not track vehicle data. LADWP does not have the
technical expertise to create, build, and maintain a GPS vehicle telematics program
essential to achieve long-term fleet efficiency, cost savings, electric vehicle transition
identification, and regulatory compliance.

emissions, vehicle availability, worker safety (lone worker), and implement
improvements in dispatching vehicles by various user groups more efficiently. The
collection of vehicle emission compliance testing will result in reduced labor hours as
vehicles equipped with GPS vehicle telematics programs will not require to be physically
tested. Samsara will be the unified enterprise vehicle/equipment GPS platform for all
divisions within LADWP. The vehicle telematic data will be utilized by Fleet Services to
locate vehicles if stolen and share the real time information with law enforcement to help
facilitate recovery. The data collected will also help to track vehicle emissions more
accurately and to help identify vehicles in our fleet that may be best suited for possible
EV replacement.

SUBJECT: Contract No. 8073 for Gas Turbine and Generator Equipment
Manufacturing Slot Reservation for Scattergood Generating Station Units
1 and 2 Green Hydrogen-Ready Modernization Project with GE Vernova
Operations LLC.
SUMMARY
The proposed Contract No. 8073 (Contract) is a single source procurement to secure
generator equipment manufacturing reservation slot for the Scattergood Generating
Station (SGS) Units 1 and 2 Green Hydrogen-Ready Modernization Project (Project), for
an amount not to exceed $15,000,000 (budgeted).
The Project requires the purchase of gas turbine and generator equipment capable of
utilizing renewable-derived green hydrogen fuel under currently advertised Request for
Proposal (RFP) 90815. Due to the current surge in demand for gas turbines and
generator equipment, manufacturers are experiencing extended lead times. As a result,
securing a reservation slot to prioritize LADWP’s position in the manufacturer’s
production schedule before execution of the equipment contract is essential. These
slots are secured through advance deposits to support lead time planning, which
remains dependent on the equipment contract award date. Without a reservation slot,
Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) contractors face challenges in
committing to Project schedule. The proposed Contract enables LADWP to place an
advance deposit, securing reservations for critical equipment. This would likely mitigate
the financial risk for EPC bidders and promote broader participation under RFP 90815
procurement process. Upon selection of an EPC contractor, the reservation Contract
will be reassigned under the EPC contract, allowing the contractor to utilize the reserved
slot without incurring additional upfront costs. Securing this single source Contract is
essential to ensure LADWP’s position in the manufacturer’s production schedule after
equipment contract is awarded and to maintain alignment with the Project schedule.
City Council approval is not required.
RECOMMENDATION
It is recommended that the Board of Water and Power Commissioners (Board) adopt
the attached Resolution authorizing the award of the Agreement to GE Vernova
Operations LLC (GE Vernova).
ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED
An alternative approach would be to proceed with the currently advertised RFP process
to select an EPC contractor for the procurement and installation of the combined cycle.
However, delaying the reservation of equipment slots until after the EPC contract is
awarded or procuring the equipment without any reservation slot would likely push
delivery timelines beyond Project completion date.
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
This Contract is for one-time purchase and is budgeted, The Contract expenditure will
not exceed $15,000,000.
BACKGROUND
On February 21, 2023, City Council approved Ordinance No.1877668 authorizing the
Board of Water and Power Commissioners to award an agreement pursuant to a
competitive-sealed proposal method for the Project.
The Project is essential to ensure compliance with the California State Water Resources
Control Board, which mandates the elimination of the use of once-through cooling
(OTC). It also supports the South Coast Air Quality Management District in reducing air
pollutant emissions in the South Coast Air Basin. Additionally, the Project also facilitates
compliance with Senate Bill 100 to have eligible renewable energy resources and zero-
carbon resources supply 100 percent of retail sales of electricity to California end-use
customers and 100 percent of electricity procured to serve all state agencies by 2045.
RFP No. 90815 has been publicly advertised since November 13, 2024, however
LADWP received no bids from EPC contractors as of today. To better understand the
underlying reasons, LADWP engaged with market participants and identified that
current supply chain constraints and equipment procurement risks were major
deterrents. To mitigate these risks and improve project viability, participants
recommended that LADWP secure a manufacturing slot reservation agreement prior to
awarding the EPC contract. Based on feedback received from potential participants, the
Contract No. 8073/December 22, 2025 Page 2
slot reservation fee for gas turbine equipment could range from $15 million to $26
million. This wide range reflects current market volatility and supply chain constraints,
further complicating early financial commitments for EPC contractors. LADWP reached
out to all three major Original Equipment Manufacturers identified as potential gas
turbine manufacturers for the Project, resulting from responses to a green hydrogen-
focused Request for Information. GE Vernova was the only vendor willing to offer a
manufacturing slot for LADWP, despite high market demand. Their offer, priced at
$15 million, secures LADWP’s position in the manufacturer’s production schedule after
equipment contract is awarded. Based on market information this is on the very low end
of similar reservation slot offers. This exception was made largely due to LADWP’s
longstanding working relationship with GE, which helped secure priority access under
otherwise constrained supply conditions.
In addition, the entire LADWP in-basin fleet, including SGS, currently operates with GE
Vernova equipment. Standardizing the manufacturer across the fleet enables significant
cost savings through shared spare parts inventory, existing tooling, and continued use
of the current GE Vernova service agreement. Moreover, LADWP personnel are already
trained and proficient in GE Vernova turbine controls, mechanical systems, and
maintenance procedures. Maintaining the same equipment platform reduces retraining
needs, minimizes risks associated with the learning curve, and supports operational
continuity.
Installation of the new combined cycle at SGS is crucial to maintain grid reliability in the
Westside service area, which supports essential infrastructures including Los Angeles
International Airport and the Hyperion Water Reclamation Plant. The mandated
retirement of SGS Units 1 and 2 under the OTC policy before the commissioning of the
new combined cycle facility will result in generation shortage and will likely compromise
service reliability for key facilities and surrounding communities. It is essential to install
the new combined cycle before the OTC mandate takes effect or minimize the gap
between the retirement of Units 1 and 2 and the installation of the new combined cycle
to ensure reliable service to key facilities and the surrounding Westside area. Therefore,
accelerated action and coordination are essential to safeguard reliability and meet
regulatory obligations.
The schedule and financial requirements tied to equipment procurement impose a
significant strain on EPC contractors. To address these concerns and reduce obstacles
for potential bidders, LADWP requests a single source Contract with GE Vernova to
secure a reservation slot.
ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION
Determine item is in compliance with California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
Guidelines Sections 15080-15097 (Environmental Impact Report [EIR] previously
adopted). In accordance with CEQA, an EIR was prepared to evaluate and disclose the
Contract No. 8073/December 22, 2025 Page 3
potential environmental impacts associated with the construction and operation of the
SGS Units 1 and 2 Green Hydrogen-Ready Modernization Project. On October 28,
2025, the Board certified the EIR; adopted the Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting
Program, Findings of Fact and Statement of Overriding Considerations; and approved
the Project.

legality.

SUBJECT: Agreement No. 47044 for Proprietary Professional, Technical, and Repair
Services and Parts with GE Vernova International, LLC
SUMMARY
The proposed sole source Agreement No. 47044 (Agreement) with GE Vernova
International, LLC (GEVINT) is required to provide and deliver proprietary professional
services, technical services, repair services, and parts. The term of the Agreement
spans five years from the date of execution, with a budgeted not-to-exceed amount of
$250,000,000.
The services and parts furnished under the Agreement are specifically intended to
enhance the reliability and availability of the Los Angeles Department of Water and
Power’s (LADWP) steam, gas, and wind electricity generating fleet. GEVINT has
proprietary expertise that enables them to deliver professional and technical support
necessary for the proper maintenance and repair of highly complex machinery and
equipment. In addition to their specialized knowledge, GEVINT can furnish the original
equipment manufacturer (OEM) parts for their turbine generator units. These services
and parts are essential for supporting continued maintenance, scheduled outages,
responding to forced outages, performing repairs, and implementing upgrades. The
activities will maintain LADWP’s ability to deliver reliable electrical service to the City of
Los Angeles, thereby supporting the City of Los Angeles’ ongoing energy needs.
To maintain uninterrupted support from GEVINT, LADWP will issue Purchase Order
(PO) No. 49849-7 for a term of two months and an amount not to exceed $150,000.
Upon the Board of Water and Power Commissioners’ approval of the Agreement, the
PO will be terminated, and all used funds and time will be deducted from the
Agreement.
As mentioned above, this Agreement will expire five years from the date of execution
less any time expended under PO 49849-7.
Los Angeles City Council approval is not required.
RECOMMENDATION
It is recommended that the Board of Water and Power Commissioners (Board) adopt
the attached Resolution authorizing the execution of the Agreement with GEVINT.
ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED
The alternative to entering into this Agreement is to handle one-time sole source
requests for the necessary services and parts on a case-by-case basis. Each of these
individual work requests would require approval from the Board and would incur an
additional cost per request. This piecemeal approach is not only inefficient but also
introduces significant risks. Processing sole source requests for each incident would
inevitably cause delays in addressing service needs. These delays could lead to
prolonged unit outages, resulting in electric system instability. The extended outages
would also contribute to considerable revenue losses and additional expenses incurred
for the organization. In addition, the case-by-case request process may jeopardize
compliance with electric reliability standards. Failure to maintain compliance could
expose the organization to fines and other regulatory penalties.
GEVINT, as the original equipment manufacturer, is uniquely qualified to perform the
specialized services required under this Agreement. The highly specialized nature of the
procedures and technologies, coupled with the proprietary information, equipment, and
methods involved, makes it infeasible to train LADWP personnel. These limitations
prevent internal staff from obtaining the necessary expertise required to perform the
work.
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
The Agreement is for a term of five years with a not-to-exceed amount of $250,000,000,
which is budgeted.
Funds will be utilized on an as-needed basis through the issuance of separately
managed Task Orders.
BACKGROUND
LADWP owns, operates, and maintains GEVINT-manufactured steam, gas, and wind
units at its electricity-generating facilities. To provide reliable electricity to the City of
Los Angeles, LADWP must conduct scheduled outages for the inspection, maintenance,
Agreement No. 47044 for Proprietary Professional, Technical, and Repair Services and Parts Page 2
with GE Vernova International, LLC / September 4, 2026
and repair of its units. LADWP must also repair the units during forced outages when
the units unexpectedly fail.
A majority of LADWP owned in-basin and all LADWP’s wind units were manufactured
by GEVINT, who has provided services and parts since commissioning and continues to
provide support to LADWP to ensure reliability of the grid. These services include
proprietary professional and technical assistance for inspections, diagnostics,
troubleshooting, recommendations, repairs, disassembly and reassembly, equipment
tuning, and regulatory compliance testing. The expertise of the firm, through its
professional, technical, and repair services, will provide the units with the required levels
of reliability and availability.
This Agreement is critical for the in-basin units that provide the firm capacity needed to
maintain a reliable and resilient electric system. The locally based generation becomes
especially important when LADWP’s electricity import capabilities are reduced due to
wildfires and other contingencies. Additionally, the Los Angeles 100% Renewable
Energy Study (LA100) substantiated that the electric system will continue to rely on in-
basin firm capacity generation sources, while LADWP achieves higher levels of
renewable energy penetration.
When one of LADWP’s steam or gas units is out of service for repairs, it could cost
LADWP up to $9,200,000 per day per unavailable unit (depending upon the capacity of
the unit and electricity market conditions) in lost revenue and purchase of make-up
power. This Agreement will lessen the financial impacts from lost revenue and incurred
expenses associated with forced outages and scheduled outages by bringing the units
back in service as fast as possible. Through this Agreement, field engineers and
technicians can be immediately contacted and brought on site to provide the proprietary
services and parts necessary to restore the units to service. This Agreement is
especially important for performing emergency repairs during unexpected, forced
outages.
To fully support LADWP’s outages for scheduled inspections, repairs, and forced
outages requiring emergency repairs, GEVINT may furnish repair services, craft labor
services, and specialty technical and professional services for non-GEVINT equipment,
hardware, or components indirectly tied to GEVINT steam, gas, and wind turbine-
generators. These support services may be provided on an as-needed basis, limited to
ten percent of the contract value. The services are necessary to minimize the impact on
outage timelines and durations when discovery work stemming from non-GEVINT
equipment requires immediate attention to allow the return of the GEVINT turbine-
generators back to service without delay.
The work performed under this Agreement will be assigned using a Task Order system.
The Task Order(s) will be issued by the Contract Administrator, and the work performed

environment do not meet that definition. Therefore, this Agreement with GE Vernova for

Resolution No. ____________
WHEREAS, the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) proposes to
enter into Agreement No. 47982 (Agreement) with Slalom, Inc. (Slalom) to provide staff
augmentation services for a term of three years; and
WHEREAS, LADWP requires a single-source agreement with Slalom due to its unique
expertise in emergency management modernization, IT strategy, data and analytics
integration, and Office of Emergency Management (OEM) operational planning, which
are essential to meeting immediate operational deadlines and regulatory requirements;
and
WHEREAS, Slalom has reviewed the services to be provided and incorporated in this
Agreement, and represents that it has the qualities, expertise, skills, and abilities to
perform such work.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that LADWP proposes to enter into the
Agreement with Slalom for an amount not to exceed $6,106,969.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that, pursuant to City Charter Section 1022, the Board of
Water and Power Commissioners (Board) finds that it is more feasible to have the work
performed by an independent contractor.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Agreement, approved as to form and legality by
the City Attorney and filed with the Secretary of the Board, is hereby approved.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Chief Accounting Employee of LADWP, upon
proper certification, is authorized and directed to draw demands on the Power and
Water Revenue Funds, in accordance with the terms of this contract awarded pursuant
to the Agreement and this Resolution.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the President, or Vice President, or the General
Manager, or such person as the General Manager shall designate in writing, and the
Secretary, Assistant Secretary, or the Acting Secretary of the Board are hereby
authorized and directed to execute said Agreement for and on behalf of LADWP.
I HEREBY CERTIFY that the foregoing is a full, true, and correct copy of the Resolution
adopted by the Board of the City of Los Angeles at its meeting held
_____________________
Secretary

RESOLUTION NO. ___________________
BOARD LETTER APPROVAL
JOHN A. SMITH JANISSE QUIÑONES
Chief Administrative Officer Chief Executive Officer and Chief Engineer
DATE: July 14, 2025
SUBJECT: Contract No. 0676 – GPS and OEM Telematics Hardware,
Subscriptions, and Integration with Samsara Networks, Inc.
SUMMARY
The proposed Contract No. 0676 (Contract) is to furnish and deliver GPS and OEM
telematics hardware, subscriptions, and integration for a term of five years, for a
cumulative estimated expenditure of $9,081,701, and for a cumulative amount not to
exceed $11,352,127 (budgeted). The Contract is a result of a competitive bid process.
The Contract will allow Fleet and Aviation Services (Fleet Services) to incorporate GPS
and vehicle telematics to effectively monitor vehicle data, predictive analytics, vehicle
utilization, electric vehicle (EV) charging data, and emissions data. The emissions
telematics data will be used to meet regulatory compliance testing requirements for
agencies like the California Bureau of Automotive Repair Testing Program (BAR CTP),
California Bureau of Automotive Repair Clean Truck Check Heavy Duty Inspection
(Clean Truck Check HD I/M), and other regulatory agencies.
City Council approval is not required.
RECOMMENDATION
It is recommended that the Board of Water and Power Commissioners (Board) adopt
the attached Resolution authorizing the award of Contract No. 0676 to Samsara
Networks, Inc. (Samsara), the lowest responsive bidder for Group A and B.
ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED
No alternatives were considered at this time.
Fleet Services will continue as is and not track vehicle data. LADWP does not
